reported.title: kth_number drops pivot-equal elements, crashes on duplicates

reported.claim: When both inputs are already square, the function returns the two input matrices wrapped in a list instead of their product.
reported.title: strassen returns inputs instead of product for square matrices

reported.claim: The first element is stored at tail[-1] instead of tail[0], so tail[0] starts as 0 and a later smaller value wrongly extends the subsequence.
reported.title: LIS length stores first element at tail[-1]

reported.claim: For input 0 the function returns 1, but zero needs no squares, and the table's own base case answers[0] = 0 shows the answer should be 0.
reported.title: minimum squares returns 1 for input 0

reported.claim: When the string character is a literal '*' and the pattern character is the '*' wildcard, the equality test `p_char in (s_char, "?")` matches first, so the wildcard branch is skipped and the DP takes the wrong value.
reported.title: wildcard is_match mishandles literal '*' in string

reported.claim: The validity check uses `and`, so it only rejects when both resistances are non-positive; a single non-positive resistance is accepted even though the error message says all values must be positive.
reported.expected: ValueError: All values must be positive
reported.title: astable_duty_cycle validity check uses and

reported.claim: Reactive power should be apparent_power * sqrt(1 - pf**2), but the code uses sqrt(1 + pf**2), which gives wrong values for any nonzero power factor.
reported.title: reactive_power uses sqrt(1 + pf^2)

reported.claim: The loop stops at len(price_series) - 1, so the output has one element fewer than the input series and the last observation is never differentiated.
reported.expected: A list of length 4 (two leading nan values followed by two computed values)
reported.title: fracdiff_fixedwindow omits last observation

reported.claim: The longitude check omits `not` on the second clause, so a valid lon2 inside [-180, 180] triggers the 'Longitude must be between -180 and 180 degrees' error while an out-of-range lon2 is accepted.
reported.expected: A positive distance of roughly 1.11e6 metres (about 10 degrees of longitude at the equator), not a ValueError.
reported.title: Lambert distance longitude check missing not

reported.claim: The lower-hull turn test passes the arguments in the wrong order (origin is lower_hull[-1] instead of lower_hull[-2]), which flips the orientation sign, so non-hull points are kept on the lower chain.
reported.title: monotone_chain lower hull turn test argument order wrong

reported.claim: The vertical-edge check compares v3.y with v2.y where it should compare v3.x with v2.x, so a valid triangle with v1 and v2 sharing an x-coordinate reaches the slope computation on line 67 and crashes with ZeroDivisionError.
reported.expected: A Triangle object is constructed without error
reported.title: Triangle vertical-edge check compares y instead of x

reported.claim: bfs indexes self.vertices[vertex] directly, so any vertex with no outgoing edges (a sink, such as the end of a single edge) raises KeyError instead of being visited and contributing an empty neighbour list.
reported.failing_call: Graph().add_edge(0, 1) or Graph.bfs on a graph built by g = Graph(); g.add_edge(0, 1); g.bfs(1)
reported.title: Graph.bfs raises KeyError for sink vertices

reported.claim: `set(start)` builds a set of the characters of the start node instead of a set containing the node, so multi-character node names that equal a neighbour's characters are wrongly treated as visited and the target is never reached.
reported.title: bfs_shortest_path_distance set(start) splits node name

reported.claim: The recursive result is discarded (`if not ...: pass`), so a non-bipartite graph whose odd cycle is found deeper in the recursion is still reported as bipartite.
reported.title: is_bipartite_dfs discards recursive result

reported.claim: `set(start)` splits the starting vertex string into its characters, so a multi-character vertex name is never added as a whole and the result contains wrong entries.
reported.title: depth_first_search set(start) splits vertex name

reported.claim: When exactly two vertices have odd degree the function should return type 2 (Euler path), but the `if odd_degree_nodes == 2: pass` branch does nothing, so it falls through and returns 3 (not Eulerian).
reported.title: check_circuit_or_path never returns Euler path type

reported.claim: The function returns the integer n instead of the donor-to-recipient matching it is documented to return (donor_record or rec_record).
reported.title: stable_matching returns n instead of matching

reported.claim: Counter(graph.get_nodes()) starts every node at a count of 1 rather than 0, so visit counts are inflated by one for each node.
reported.title: markov chain visit counts inflated by one

reported.claim: The first cell of each row is decremented by the cell above instead of incremented, so path sums are wrong whenever more than one row exists.
reported.title: minimum_path_sum fill_row subtracts instead of adds

reported.claim: The remaining capacity subtracts the weight of item counter+1 (the next item, possibly out of range) instead of the current item's weight at counter-1.
reported.title: knapsack_recur subtracts wrong item's weight

reported.claim: Assigning `row -= 1` inside a `for row in range(rank)` loop does nothing, so after a column is dropped the same row is never rechecked against the new column; the rank comes out too low.
reported.title: rank_of_matrix row -= 1 has no effect in for loop

reported.claim: The reflection matrix diagonal should be 2*c*c-1 and 2*s*s-1 (2 times the projection minus identity), but the code uses 2*c-1 and 2*s-1, which is inconsistent with projection() and with the reflection formula.
reported.title: reflection matrix diagonal uses 2c-1 instead of 2c^2-1

reported.claim: The function returns the leftover loop variable item_tuple instead of the pruned candidate list, and raises NameError when candidates is empty.
reported.title: apriori prune returns loop variable instead of list

reported.claim: inc subtracts num_occur from the count instead of adding it, so repeated transactions reduce node counts when update_tree increments an existing node.
reported.expected: None, with the node's count becoming 3
reported.title: TreeNode.inc subtracts occurrences

reported.claim: The epsilon is subtracted inside the square root instead of added as the docstring specifies, so a zero moving average makes math.sqrt receive a negative number and crash.
reported.title: rmsprop subtracts epsilon inside sqrt

reported.claim: The function computes Heron's formula into `area` but returns side2 instead of the area.
reported.title: area_triangle_three_sides returns side2

reported.claim: The origin latitude is read from origin[-1] (the longitude) instead of origin[0], so the wrong coordinates are used for the starting point.
reported.title: initial_bearing reads origin longitude as latitude

reported.claim: The result starts as an unreduced 1, so when exponent is 0 the function returns 1 even when modulus is 1, where a^0 % 1 should be 0.
reported.title: binary_exp_mod_iterative wrong for modulus 1 exponent 0

reported.claim: Multiplying the float by 10**digits and truncating with int() can lose precision (e.g. 0.29*100 is 28.999999999999996), giving a wrong numerator.
reported.title: decimal_to_fraction float truncation loses precision

reported.claim: The isinstance(edge, int) check rejects float edge lengths, although the docstring declares edge as a float.
reported.expected: A positive float surface area (about 0.5 * 516.143... scaled by 2.5**2, i.e. about 80.4).
reported.title: dodecahedron_surface_area rejects float edges

reported.claim: The vertical-line branch returns C = p1[0], but the line x = p1[0] written in the form A*x + B*y + C = 0 with A=1, B=0 needs C = -p1[0], so segment_intersection gives the wrong x for vertical lines.
reported.title: line_coefficients wrong sign of C for vertical lines

reported.claim: Using math.log10 for the digit count gives floating-point errors near powers of ten, so 10**15 - 1 is reported as 16 digits instead of 15.
reported.title: num_digits_fast log10 floating-point errors

reported.claim: The trapezoid term takes abs(fx2 + fx1), so segments where the curve is negative add positive area instead of signed area.
reported.title: trapezoidal_area uses abs, losing sign

reported.claim: The loop ends with prev_num holding P(n), but the function returns prev_prev_num, which holds P(n-1), so every subscript of 2 or more gives the previous Pell number.
reported.title: pell_number_iterative returns P(n-1)

reported.claim: The float cube root n ** (1/3) is inexact (64 ** (1/3) is 3.9999999999999996), so the cube check fails for some true perfect cubes.
reported.title: perfect_cube float cube root inexact

reported.claim: The guard `max_n > 2` skips yielding 2 when max_n is exactly 2, although 2 is prime and lies within the range up to max_n.
reported.title: fast_primes skips 2 when max_n is 2

reported.claim: The accumulator starts at 1 instead of 0, so every mean is inflated by 1/len(series).
reported.title: arithmetic_mean accumulator starts at 1

reported.claim: The base case B(0)=1 is written to bell[-1] (the last element) instead of bell[0], so the first entry stays 0 and all later Bell numbers are wrong.
reported.title: bell_numbers writes base case to bell[-1]

reported.claim: The split range stops one short: it should run up to digits (inclusive of the last split), so squares with only two digits such as 81 (for 9) are never split and 9 is wrongly reported as not Kaprekar.
reported.title: is_kaprekar split range stops one short

reported.claim: The search starts at index 1, so row 0 is never checked and a value present only in the first row is reported as not found.
reported.title: mat_bin_search skips row 0

reported.claim: The empty-input guard tests `matrix_b` instead of `not matrix_b`, so any call with a non-empty `matrix_b` returns [] instead of the Kronecker product.
reported.title: kronecker_product empty guard wrong

reported.claim: Setting next_row = current_row aliases the two buffers, so after the first row the diagonal and bottom reads see values already overwritten in the current row, giving too-large square sizes.
reported.title: largest_square space-optimized aliases row buffers

reported.claim: The shape check compares rows of A with columns of B and columns of A with rows of B, so it rejects valid same-shape non-square operands, breaking add and subtract (and multiply for many valid inputs).
reported.title: _verify_matrix_sizes compares wrong dimensions

reported.claim: The range stops one short (len(...) - 1), so the last resource column is dropped from the allocated-resource totals.
reported.title: BankersAlgorithm drops last resource column

reported.claim: The branch conditions are inverted: any truthy n (including positive capacities) sets the capacity to sys.maxsize, so the requested capacity is ignored, and the n < 0 ValueError is unreachable.
reported.title: LRUCache.__init__ branch conditions inverted

reported.claim: The swap in _position_node sets previous_node.next to the wrong node and never links the node before the swapped pair back to the moved node, so the list is corrupted whenever a node must move forward.
reported.title: LFU _position_node swap corrupts list links

reported.claim: The function uses the global p4_table, but p4_table is only defined inside the __main__ block, so calling function() from an imported module raises NameError.
reported.title: sdes function depends on p4_table defined only in __main__

reported.claim: The check `tangential_force <= 0` rejects a tangential force of zero, but zero is a valid input that the `elif tangential_force == 0` branch is meant to handle, so the function wrongly raises an error.
reported.title: shear_stress rejects zero tangential force

reported.claim: The deadline check uses the enumerate position of every task, including rejected ones, so a rejected task still consumes a time slot and wrongly blocks later tasks; it should use the count of tasks already accepted.
reported.title: max_tasks rejected tasks consume time slot

reported.claim: When a process arrives after the current time, the current time should be set to the arrival time, but the code adds the arrival time to the current time, so the clock is wrong.
reported.title: MLFQ first_come_first_served adds arrival time instead of setting

reported.claim: When a process arrives after the current time, the current time is increased by the arrival time instead of being set to it, so the simulated clock is wrong.
reported.title: MLFQ round_robin adds arrival time instead of setting

reported.claim: When the search range shrinks to a single element and the target is absent, the recursion moves high to -1, which fails the bounds check and raises ValueError instead of returning -1.
reported.title: rec_linear_search raises ValueError when target absent

reported.claim: For full groups it slices arr[i:] (the whole remainder) instead of the five-element window arr[i:i+5], so the medians list is built from the wrong groups and the returned pivot is wrong.
reported.title: median_of_medians slices remainder instead of 5-element window

reported.claim: For an empty input, block_size becomes 0 and range(0, 0, 0) raises ValueError, although the `if n <= 1: pass` guard suggests empty input was meant to return an empty list.
reported.title: kirkpatrick_reisch_sort crashes on empty input

reported.claim: The final insertion loop runs len(sorted_list_2d)+1 times, so it indexes sorted_list_2d one past its end and raises IndexError for any input of length 4 or more with no leftover odd item; it also reinserts the larger partner (index 1) that is already in result instead of the pending smaller element.
reported.title: merge_insertion_sort loop overruns, IndexError for length 4+

reported.claim: The zeros bucket is recursed with bit_position + 1 instead of bit_position - 1, so bit positions move upward and a bucket of equal numbers with a zero bit never reaches the bit_position == 0 base case, causing unbounded recursion.
reported.title: msd_radix_sort recurses zeros bucket with wrong bit position

reported.claim: The comparison uses collection[i - 1] < collection[i] but the swap is applied to positions i and i + 1, so pairs are compared and swapped inconsistently and the list is not sorted.
reported.title: odd_even_transposition compares and swaps different positions

reported.claim: The length test is combined with `or` instead of `and`, so any 13-digit barcode is reported valid without checking its check digit.
reported.title: barcode is_valid uses or, skipping check digit

reported.claim: The guard `m >= len(text)` returns -1 when the pattern is exactly as long as the text, even though an exact match should be found at index 0.
reported.title: bitap_string_match fails when pattern equals text length

reported.claim: When the weighted subtotal is divisible by 10 the checksum is computed as 10 instead of 0, so a valid PESEL with check digit 0 is rejected.
reported.title: Polish national ID checksum gives 10 instead of 0

reported.claim: The swap condition uses `<=`, so two non-empty words of equal length swap back and forth forever and eventually raise RecursionError instead of returning the distance.
reported.title: levenshtein_distance_optimized infinite recursion on equal lengths

reported.claim: The function returns the leftover loop variable `word` (the last word of the sentence) instead of the `occurrence` dictionary of counts that its name and docstring describe.
reported.title: word_occurrence returns last word instead of counts
